## ISL Exercise 5.4.2 (20pts)



:::{.callout-note}
As we learned the key to bagging is that trees are
repeatedly fit to bootstrapped subsets of the observations. This shows
that on average, each bagged tree makes use of around two-thirds of the
observations.
:::


## TCGA-BRCA via recount3

This is a self-contained script that runs the complete analysis:

- download and define labels
- do unsupervised filtering 
- run fold-specific supervised screening using either limma or absolute correlation on VST values
- fit within each fold
  + Ridge, lasso, elastic net (pick one)
  + Random Forest, Boosting Trees (pick one)
- evaluate via outer CV AUC 
- summarize stability by counting how often genes are screened.

:::{.callout-note}
This might be a long-running script (several hours). These are pseudo-code.  You should adapt it to your own needs, e.g., by reducing the number of folds, tuning grid size, etc.
:::

```{r, eval = F}
## ============================================================
## Tidymodels version scaffold:
## - outer CV with rsample
## - fold-specific preprocessing + screening (train-only)
## - compare: elastic net vs random forest vs xgboost
## ============================================================

## ---- packages ----
library(tidymodels)
library(matrixStats)
library(DESeq2)
library(edgeR)
library(limma)

# helpers;  
# - first_col_match()
# - screen_sis_abs_cor()
# - screen_limma_p()

## ---- helper: fold preprocessing + screening (train-only) ----
prep_rnaseq_split <- function(split,
                              counts_mat,              # genes x samples
                              sample_df,               # sample_id + class
                              screen = c("limma", "sis"),
                              cpm_thresh = 1,
                              min_samples = 10,
                              var_quantile = 0.50,
                              top_k = 500) {

  screen <- match.arg(screen)

  tr <- analysis(split)
  te <- assessment(split)

  tr_ids <- tr$sample_id
  te_ids <- te$sample_id

  # subset counts
  counts_tr <- counts_mat[, tr_ids, drop = FALSE]
  counts_te <- counts_mat[, te_ids, drop = FALSE]

  y_tr <- droplevels(tr$class)
  y_te <- droplevels(te$class)

  # (a) TRAIN-only CPM filter
  cpm_tr <- edgeR::cpm(counts_tr)
  keep <- rowSums(cpm_tr > cpm_thresh) >= min_samples

  ct_tr <- counts_tr[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  ct_te <- counts_te[rownames(ct_tr), , drop = FALSE]

  # (b) VST (design ~ 1) — computed separately on train and test
  # NOTE: This is “okay-ish” for teaching, but you can discuss what “proper”
  # out-of-sample transforms mean in RNA-seq.
  dds_tr <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = ct_tr,
    colData   = data.frame(row.names = colnames(ct_tr)),
    design    = ~ 1
  ) |> estimateSizeFactors()

  Xtr <- assay(vst(dds_tr, blind = TRUE))  # genes x samples

  dds_te <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = ct_te,
    colData   = data.frame(row.names = colnames(ct_te)),
    design    = ~ 1
  ) |> estimateSizeFactors()

  Xte <- assay(vst(dds_te, blind = TRUE))

  # (c) TRAIN-only variance filter
  v <- matrixStats::rowVars(Xtr)
  keep_v <- v >= quantile(v, var_quantile)
  Xtr_v <- Xtr[keep_v, , drop = FALSE]
  Xte_v <- Xte[rownames(Xtr_v), , drop = FALSE]

  # (d) Screening
  sel_genes <-
    if (screen == "limma") {
      screen_limma_p(Xtr_v, y_tr, top_k = top_k)
    } else {
      screen_sis_abs_cor(Xtr_v, y_tr, top_k = top_k)
    }

  # (e) Return train/test tibbles (samples in rows, genes in columns)
  x_tr <- t(Xtr_v[sel_genes, , drop = FALSE]) |> as.data.frame() |> as_tibble()
  x_te <- t(Xte_v[sel_genes, , drop = FALSE]) |> as.data.frame() |> as_tibble()

  train_tbl <- bind_cols(tibble(class = y_tr), x_tr)
  test_tbl  <- bind_cols(tibble(class = y_te), x_te)

  list(
    train = train_tbl,
    test  = test_tbl,
    selected_genes = sel_genes
  )
}

## ---- model specs (students will compare these) ----
spec_enet <-
  logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

spec_rf <-
  rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 1000, min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

spec_xgb <-
  boost_tree(
    mtry = tune(),
    trees = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune(),
    learn_rate = tune(),
    min_n = tune(),
    loss_reduction = tune(),
    sample_size = tune()
  ) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

## ---- recipe (lightweight; selection already happened) ----
base_rec <- function(df) {
  recipe(class ~ ., data = df) %>%
    step_zv(all_predictors())
  # Optional: step_normalize(all_predictors())  # helpful for glmnet
}

## ---- tuning grids (keep small for homework runtime) ----
grid_enet <- grid_regular(
  penalty(range = c(-4, 0)),   # 1e-4 to 1
  mixture(),
  levels = c(10, 6)
)

# These get finalized per-fold because mtry depends on #predictors
grid_rf <- function(train_df) {
  params <- parameters(
    finalize(mtry(), train_df),
    min_n()
  )
  grid_latin_hypercube(params, size = 15)
}

grid_xgb <- function(train_df) {
  params <- parameters(
    finalize(mtry(), train_df),
    trees(),
    tree_depth(),
    learn_rate(),
    min_n(),
    loss_reduction(),
    sample_size = sample_prop()
  )
  grid_latin_hypercube(params, size = 20)
}

## ---- inner-tune + outer-test evaluation (one split, one screen, one model) ----
fit_one_outer <- function(split,
                          counts_mat,
                          screen = c("limma", "sis"),
                          model = c("enet", "rf", "xgb"),
                          top_k = 500,
                          v_inner = 5) {

  screen <- match.arg(screen)
  model  <- match.arg(model)

  pre <- prep_rnaseq_split(
    split = split,
    counts_mat = counts_mat,
    sample_df = NULL,       # not used; kept in signature if you want it later
    screen = screen,
    top_k = top_k
  )

  train_df <- pre$train
  test_df  <- pre$test

  # inner CV for tuning
  inner_rs <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = v_inner, strata = class)

  wf <-
    workflow() %>%
    add_recipe(base_rec(train_df)) %>%
    add_model(
      switch(model,
        enet = spec_enet,
        rf   = spec_rf,
        xgb  = spec_xgb
      )
    )

  # pick grid by model
  grid <-
    switch(model,
      enet = grid_enet,
      rf   = grid_rf(train_df),
      xgb  = grid_xgb(train_df)
    )

  metr <- metric_set(roc_auc)

  tuned <- tune_grid(
    wf,
    resamples = inner_rs,
    grid = grid,
    metrics = metr,
    control = control_grid(save_pred = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  )

  best <- select_best(tuned, metric = "roc_auc")
  final_wf <- finalize_workflow(wf, best)

  final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = train_df)

  # predictions on outer test fold
  probs <- predict(final_fit, new_data = test_df, type = "prob") %>%
    bind_cols(test_df %>% select(class))

  # IMPORTANT: your factor levels are c("Tumor","Normal") so "Normal" is the 2nd level
  auc <- roc_auc(probs, truth = class, .pred_Normal, event_level = "second") %>%
    dplyr::pull(.estimate)

  tibble(
    screen = screen,
    model  = model,
    roc_auc = auc,
    selected_genes = list(pre$selected_genes)
  )
}

## ---- outer resampling (students should own this part) ----
# sample_df should exist from your earlier recount3 code:
# sample_df <- tibble(sample_id = colnames(counts_f), class = y)

# NOTE: rsample splits need a data frame; we resample sample_df, then index counts by sample_id
outer_rs <- vfold_cv(sample_df, v = 5, repeats = 3, strata = class)

# Run the experiment:
set.seed(1)
results <-
  crossing(
    screen = c("limma", "sis"),
    model  = c("enet", "rf", "xgb")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    res = pmap(
      list(screen, model),
      ~ map_dfr(
        outer_rs$splits,
        \(sp) fit_one_outer(
          split = sp,
          counts_mat = counts_f,
          screen = ..1,
          model  = ..2,
          top_k  = 500,
          v_inner = 5
        )
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(res)

# Summaries
results %>%
  group_by(screen, model) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_auc = mean(roc_auc),
    sd_auc   = sd(roc_auc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot
results %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = roc_auc)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ screen)

# Stability: how often selected (by screen+model)
stab <-
  results %>%
  select(screen, model, selected_genes) %>%
  unnest(selected_genes) %>%
  count(screen, model, selected_genes, sort = TRUE)

stab %>% group_by(screen, model) %>% slice_head(n = 20)
```
